subject: API 5xx/429 Spike — ByteWave production impact
messages:
From: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@bytewave.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@bytewave.ai, support@bytewave.ai
Date: 2026-07-05T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: API 5xx/429 Spike — ByteWave production impact

Evelyn —

We’re seeing a large increase in 5xx and 429 responses hitting our production integrations with Redwood starting ~07:55 PDT. Our dashboard shows about ~18% error rate across user-facing inference calls (primarily gen endpoints) and a corresponding spike in client-side timeouts (requests now taking 20–30s before failing). This is causing search result gaps and customer-facing failures for several accounts.

Quick datapoints:
- Error types: 500, 502, 504, and 429 (429 trending up).
- P50 latency: 180ms -> 1.2s; P95: 3s -> 28s over last 15m.
- Estimated affected qps: 220 -> 600 during peak.
- Earliest observed: 2026-07-05T07:55:00 PDT.

We’ve attached a short sample log segment and a few request ids. ByteWave is seeing customer escalations now — we need an ETA and mitigation ASAP. Can you confirm whether this is an internal capacity/regression issue or a known downstream outage? If you need us to throttle client retries or flip to a fallback model, we can coordinate immediately.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Chen
CTO, ByteWave

Attachment(s): bytewave_error_sample.log (text)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-05T08:18:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: API 5xx/429 Spike — ByteWave production impact

Team — forwarding an external escalation from ByteWave (see attached log). They report increasing 5xx/429 and client timeouts impacting production.

Immediate asks:
1) Engineering (David) — triage root cause (retry storm? autoscaler lag? model OOM?). Prioritize investigating worker queue/backpressure and LB 429s.
2) CS (Stephanie) — acknowledge to customer and provide a concise ETA (5–60min window) while we triage.
3) Sales/AM (Marcus) — prep for potential exec escalation and be ready to propose a goodwill credit if SLA gap confirmed.
4) Ops (Laura) — confirm if any capacity events, infra deployments, or scaling anomalies in the last 30m.

Proposed immediate mitigations to consider: temporary shedding for very large requests, enable request-level rate shed for high QPS keys, scale up pool by +30% if capacity allows, and advise ByteWave to reduce client retry aggressiveness to exponential backoff with jitter.

I’m standing by. Please post updates to this thread and to the incident channel.

—Evelyn

Quoted:
> From: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@bytewave.ai>
> Subject: API 5xx/429 Spike — ByteWave production impact
> Date: 2026-07-05 08:12:00 -0700
>
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-05T08:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: API 5xx/429 Spike — ByteWave production impact

Quick triage notes (short):
- Initial signal looks like a retry amplification pattern. Many client retry bundles are arriving in bursts — exacerbated by a small autoscaler target for the particular GPU pool serving ByteWave’s model variant.
- Control plane & infra show no ongoing hardware failures; no deployment pushed in last 45m.
- Observed: request queue depth spike and increased KV cache misses for long-context requests; that increases tail latency leading clients to retry.

Immediate actions (I’m starting now):
A) Increase pool target by +40% for the next 30m (scaling command issued, should add capacity within 6–10m).
B) Enable temporary request-shedding policy for requests > 250k tokens and a lower per-key concurrency cap (will protect cluster while we add nodes).
C) Apply a fast path patch to return 429 earlier for overloaded keys to avoid long-running slow requests (patch attached as diff).
D) Ask ByteWave to drop retries to 2 attempts with exponential backoff while we stabilize.

ETA: capacity + shedding in place within ~15–20 minutes; expect error rate to drop below 3–5% after capacity added and shedding active. Will post metrics in 10m.

-David

Attachment(s): redwood_temp_rate_limit_patch.diff
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@bytewave.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-05T08:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: API 5xx/429 Spike — ByteWave production impact

Sarah — quick update and proposed immediate plan: thank you for the signal and the logs. We’ve identified a retry-amplification + autoscaler gap as the likely root cause and have enacted short-term mitigations.

What we’ve done so far:
- Issued an autoscaler increase (+40% target) for the pool serving your model variant (David).
- Activated per-key concurrency caps and a short request-shedding rule for very large requests.
- Pushed a hotfix that makes the service return 429 earlier for overload scenarios to avoid long-running timeouts.

Customer-facing ask: please set client retry to max=2 attempts with exponential backoff and jitter for the next 30 minutes — this will greatly reduce amplification while we stabilize. If you want Redwood to perform a remote config change for your integration keys, we can coordinate a short maintenance window (we prefer customer-initiated changes for safety).

ETA: David expects the error rate to materially decline in the next 15–25 minutes and for user-facing failures to be mostly resolved within 45–60 minutes. We will send another update with metrics and a status page entry.

Immediate point of contact: me (evelyn.hart@redwood.ai). We appreciate your patience — we’re treating this as P1 for ByteWave.

—Evelyn
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-05T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: RE: API 5xx/429 Spike — ByteWave production impact (exec note)

Looping in Markus for visibility — ByteWave is a strategic mid-market customer with expansion in our pipeline. CS reports increased pressure from their ops and a few enterprise customers on their side.

Recommendation: prepare a short incident statement and offer a one-time service credit (suggest 20–30% of last month’s invoice or a usage credit) contingent on postmortem findings. Also propose a joint postmortem within 72 hours and share an initial timeline publicly on our status page.

Evelyn — can you confirm the likely RCA surface by EOD so we can finalize the credit proposal?

-Marcus
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@bytewave.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-05T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: API 5xx/429 Spike — ByteWave production impact

Sarah — final update for now:

Status: services are back to baseline. Error rate has dropped from ~18% at peak to 1.9% over the last 10 minutes; P95 latency returned to expected band. We’ve confirmed reduced tail latency after capacity increase and shedding rules were applied.

What we did:
- Scaled pool +40% and stabilized within ~9 minutes.
- Enabled per-key concurrency caps and a temporary request-shed policy for oversized requests.
- Deployed a hotfix that returns 429 earlier for overloaded keys to avoid long timeouts (diff attached).
- Recommended ByteWave lower client retry attempts to 2 with exponential backoff while we complete the postmortem.

Next steps:
- We’ll run a short follow-up exercise to tune autoscaler thresholds to avoid similar lag on sudden traffic bursts.
- Redwood will produce a postmortem draft and share within 72 hours; we’ll include timeline, RCA, and remediation plan.
- Marcus will follow up on commercial remediation (credit) based on the postmortem.

Attachments: incident_timeline.csv, postmortem-draft.md

We’ll keep the incident open until the postmortem is complete; I’ll ping you when the draft is ready. Please reach out immediately if you see any regression.

—Evelyn
